source_span: higher commodity inflation is now pulling the front end with it as the market prices a greater chance the Fed actually responds
source_chain: Geopolitical escalation pushes crude/gas/distillates higher, therefore commodity inflation pulls short-dated yields up too (not just the long end) because the market prices a higher chance the Fed hikes in response, therefore a supply shock hurts growth at the same time the Fed is pushed toward tightening, compressing multiples; invalidation: if crude/gas/product prices fall, yields stabilize and risk can recover provided NFP/CPI cooperate, but if energy keeps rising the Fed reaction function drags with it and sustained equity upside gets much harder.
pulse_chain: Energy prices spike (Brent, European gas), therefore yields rise across the curve including the short end because traders price a higher chance the Fed answers energy with a hike (attributed to Goldman's equity sales desk), therefore a supply shock slowing growth collides with tighter policy and compresses what investors pay for earnings, with the bank debate correctly split (JPM equity strategy bullish on the 'yields aren't an obstacle, less tightening than priced' logic at 65/60 OW; JPM Market Intel tactically cautious, cutting net longs; Goldman sales desk cautious on the reaction-function view; TS Lombard disputing the hike via the Dallas Fed trimmed-mean/Taylor Rule math); invalidation: energy relief lets yields stabilize and risk recover if payrolls/inflation cooperate, continued energy climb keeps the constructive case from holding, with August CPI as the decision point.
why: The pulse reproduces the note's exact mechanism (energy inflation dragging the front end via Fed-response repricing, supply shock plus tightening compressing multiples) with correct attribution to Goldman's sales desk and the same energy-price invalidation, without reversing any step or swapping the condition.
